prompts.prompt: Explain dependency injection to a non-technical project manager in about a minute.
tips: Open with a real-world analogy
Skip jargon — no 'IoC container'
End with why it helps the team

prompts.prompt: Explain what an API is to someone who has never written code.
tips: Try the restaurant-waiter analogy — or invent your own
One concrete example beats three abstract ones

prompts.prompt: Explain the difference between SQL and NoSQL databases and when you'd pick each.
tips: Structure: what each is → one strength each → a picking rule
Name a real product for each (e.g. Postgres, MongoDB)

prompts.prompt: Explain what a database index is and why queries get faster with one.
tips: The book-index analogy is your friend
Mention the write-cost trade-off for bonus depth

prompts.prompt: Explain async/await to a junior developer who only knows synchronous code.
tips: Start with WHY blocking is a problem
Use a everyday waiting situation as the analogy

prompts.prompt: Explain what caching is and one problem it can cause.
tips: Definition → example → the stale-data catch
Say 'invalidation' and smile

prompts.prompt: Explain REST versus GraphQL and when you would choose one over the other.
tips: One sentence on each before comparing
Anchor it in over-fetching / under-fetching

prompts.prompt: Explain what a closure is in JavaScript, with a simple example you describe out loud.
tips: Describe the example in words — no code on screen
Say what problem closures solve, not just the definition

prompts.prompt: Explain the difference between authentication and authorization.
tips: 'Who are you' vs 'what may you do'
One example: logging in vs an admin-only page

prompts.prompt: Explain what Docker solves, to a developer who has never used containers.
tips: Lead with the 'works on my machine' pain
Container vs VM in one sentence, no more

prompts.prompt: Explain what Angular's change detection does and why developers care about it.
tips: What triggers it → what it updates → why perf matters
Mention signals or OnPush if you know them

prompts.prompt: Explain the difference between an Observable and a Promise.
tips: One value vs a stream of values
Mention cancellation — it's the interview favourite

prompts.prompt: Explain what middleware does in ASP.NET Core using the request pipeline.
tips: Picture the request passing through checkpoints
Name two real middleware examples

prompts.prompt: Explain the difference between server-side rendering and client-side rendering.
tips: Who builds the HTML, and when?
Tie each to a benefit: SEO/first paint vs interactivity

prompts.prompt: Explain what a JOIN does in SQL and describe one type of JOIN with an example.
tips: Two small tables, one shared column — paint the picture
Pick INNER or LEFT and commit to it

prompts.prompt: Explain what React hooks are and why they replaced class components for most teams.
tips: State + lifecycle in plain functions
Name useState and useEffect with a one-line job each

prompts.prompt: Explain what technical debt is to a product owner who wants the feature yesterday.
tips: The loan analogy: borrow speed now, pay interest later
End with what you propose, not just the problem

prompts.prompt: Explain what unit tests are and why they're worth the time they take to write.
tips: Definition in one sentence, then sell the WHY
Mention the confidence-to-refactor payoff

prompts.prompt: Explain what happens between typing a URL and seeing the page.
tips: DNS → connection → request → response → render
Depth on one step beats a shallow list of ten

prompts.prompt: Explain the difference between git merge and git rebase, and your team rule for them.
tips: History shape: merge keeps it, rebase rewrites it
A team rule shows judgment, not just knowledge

prompts.prompt: Tell me about a time you disagreed with a technical decision. What did you do?
tips: Use STAR: Situation, Task, Action, Result
Own YOUR actions — say 'I', not 'we'
Land on the outcome, even if you lost the argument

prompts.prompt: Tell me about a bug that took you days to find. Walk me through how you tracked it down.
tips: The hunt is the story — narrate your reasoning
End with what you changed so it can't recur

prompts.prompt: Tell me about a time you missed a deadline. What happened and what did you learn?
tips: Own it early — no blaming
Spend most of your time on the lesson and what changed after

prompts.prompt: Describe the project you're proudest of. What was YOUR contribution?
tips: Pick ONE project, not your career summary
Numbers make it real: users, time saved, bugs cut

prompts.prompt: Tell me about a time you received tough feedback. How did you respond?
tips: Name the actual feedback — vagueness reads as dodging
Show the change in behaviour that followed

prompts.prompt: Tell me about a time you had to learn a new technology fast. How did you approach it?
tips: Your learning SYSTEM is the answer, not the tech
End with shipping something with it

prompts.prompt: Describe a time you helped a struggling teammate.
tips: Respect their dignity in the retelling
The result is their growth, not your heroics

prompts.prompt: Tell me about a production incident you were involved in. What was your role?
tips: Timeline it: detection → diagnosis → fix → prevention
Stay calm in the telling — that IS the signal

prompts.prompt: Tell me about a time you had to say no to a stakeholder.
tips: Show the trade-off you explained, not just the 'no'
Offer the alternative you gave them

prompts.prompt: Describe a time you improved something nobody asked you to improve.
tips: Why did YOU notice it?
Quantify the payoff if you can

prompts.prompt: Tell me about your biggest technical mistake and what it taught you.
tips: Pick a real one — interviewers smell fake humility
The lesson should be specific, not 'be more careful'

prompts.prompt: Tell me about a time you worked with a difficult colleague.
tips: Never trash them — describe behaviour, not character
What did YOU adjust to make it work?

prompts.prompt: Describe a time you had too much on your plate. How did you prioritize?
tips: Name your actual method: impact, deadlines, asking
Saying what you DROPPED shows real judgment

prompts.prompt: Tell me about a time a requirement changed late in development. How did you handle it?
tips: Frustration is fine to mention — dwelling on it isn't
Show the re-plan, not just the re-work

prompts.prompt: Why are you looking to leave your current role?
tips: Run TOWARD the new role, not away from the old one
One honest reason beats three polished ones

prompts.prompt: Tell me about a time you had to deliver bad news to your manager or client.
tips: Early, direct, with a plan — show that pattern
What did you propose in the same breath?

prompts.prompt: Describe a decision you made with incomplete information.
tips: Show the risk you weighed and the reversibility
It's fine if the call was wrong — the process is the answer

prompts.prompt: Where do you see yourself in three years?
tips: Ambition + realism, tied to the role you're in the room for
Growth in craft counts as much as titles

prompts.prompt: Give your daily stand-up update: what you did yesterday, what you'll do today, and one blocker.
tips: Three sentences is enough
Name the blocker AND who you need for it

prompts.prompt: Introduce yourself to a new team on your first day.
tips: Name, what you'll be working on, one human detail
Short and warm beats long and impressive

prompts.prompt: Explain to your project manager why the feature will be three days late.
tips: Lead with the new date, then the reason
Offer what you can deliver sooner

prompts.prompt: The requirements you received are vague. Ask the product owner the questions you need answered.
tips: Ask 2-3 specific questions, not 'can you clarify?'
Restate what you THINK they meant first

prompts.prompt: Push back politely on a code review comment you disagree with.
tips: Acknowledge their point before your counter
Argue the code, never the person
Offer to take it to a quick call if it drags

prompts.prompt: Explain a technical problem to a client who is not technical and is slightly upset.
tips: Empathy first, explanation second
No jargon — say what it means FOR THEM
Close with the fix and a time

prompts.prompt: Ask your manager for time to pay down technical debt in the next sprint.
tips: Frame it in THEIR currency: speed, bugs, risk
Ask for something specific and bounded

prompts.prompt: A teammate's pull request has a serious problem. Tell them about it kindly but clearly.
tips: Praise something real first — but keep it honest
Describe the impact, then suggest a direction

prompts.prompt: Summarize a one-hour architecture meeting in one minute for a colleague who missed it.
tips: Decisions first, discussion second
End with what THEY need to do, if anything

prompts.prompt: Tell the team the scope needs to be cut to hit the release date. Propose what to cut.
tips: Propose, don't just report the problem
Explain why YOUR cut hurts least

prompts.prompt: Ask a senior developer for help with something you've been stuck on for a day — without sounding lost.
tips: Show what you already tried in one breath
Ask a narrow question, not 'it doesn't work'

prompts.prompt: Hand over your in-progress work to a teammate before you leave on holiday.
tips: State: done, in-progress, next, and the one gotcha
Say where things live — branch, ticket, doc
